nodes.name: RFQ received
nodes.notes: Swap this for a Gmail/IMAP trigger once a mailbox is connected. Everything downstream reads the same fields, so the rest of the workflow does not change.

nodes.name: Freight Core — POST /ingest/rfq
nodes.notes: Retries are safe: the API keys the quote on rfq:<messageId>, and the (type, source_ref) unique index means a repeated call returns the original quote instead of issuing a second one.

nodes.name: What did it decide?
nodes.notes: The API answers 200 for all four outcomes. A refused RFQ is a business answer, not a transport failure — returning 5xx would make n8n retry a lane that will never price.

nodes.name: Quoted
nodes.notes: Next: send the quote PDF to the customer via GET /quotes/{id}/pdf. Kept out of this slice so one thing is proven at a time.

nodes.name: Hand to a person
nodes.notes: Unknown sender, or a party still under denied-party screening. Onboarding a customer automatically would mean quoting before screening resolves, which is how you price freight for a sanctioned counterparty. Next: post to the ops channel.

nodes.name: No rate for this lane
nodes.notes: The engine refuses lanes it holds no valid card for, and service levels it cannot meet. That is an answer to give the customer, not an error to retry.

nodes.name: Unrecognised status
nodes.notes: Dead letter. If the API grows a status this workflow does not know, it lands here visibly rather than being silently treated as success.
